Scene Foundation

Sky, atmosphere, terrain, lighting, shadows, grade — plus a time-of-day and weather system so one zone spans both reference art directions. The dependency root; every other system renders on top of this.

Refining iteration 2

Rubric sectionScoreRead
R1 Lighting & tonemapping 2.8 Sky scattering, IBL ambient and colour space all read PS4-tier. Held back by a flat white clipped patch around the sun disc in grazing and dawn.
R2 Shadows & contact 2.3 Contact darkening under rocks is convincing (3/4). Killed by R2.2 at 1/4 — a mechanically regular corduroy ripple raked across the midground in 7 of 9 shots.
R3 Terrain & world scale 2.2 Layered silhouettes and aerial perspective are genuine strengths (3/4 each). Ground detail at eye height scored 1/4 — the same ripple artifact.
R4 Foliage & density 1.6 Weakest section. Backlit translucency 1/4 (scrub reads as flat opaque silhouettes), wind 1/4 (no coherent gust direction), density countable rather than a field.
R5 Post & atmosphere 2.5 Per-weather grade praised as genuinely PS4-tier and clearly differentiated. Bloom bleeds into non-HDR sky around the sun.
R6 Time-of-day & weather 2.2 Night (3/4) and golden hour (3/4) are authored and hold up. Overcast nearly shapeless (1/4) and storm wetness reads as a colour shift, not water (1/4).

ROUND 2 LANDED. The corduroy ripple both critics independently traced to macRelief() is gone from every shot. Scatter density is up 3-4x inside the playable bowl, storm now shows real standing water, and backlit scrub genuinely glows gold against the dark hillside — the FFXV money shot works. Character System

Original humanoid mesh, skeleton, skinning, PBR materials, idle animation. No copyrighted likeness or ripped rig.

Refining iteration 2
not yet scored

Critic — biggest gap

BODY FIXED, FACE NOT. Two agents worked the mesh concurrently and found three separate bugs between them: (1) surface-nets emitted every dual quad with the same winding regardless of the crossing direction, so roughly half of every mesh came out inverted — you were seeing through the inverted half into the interior; (2) material.js quoted procedural detail in cycles per metre on a 1.8m character, putting cloth weave at a 1.06mm period, past Nyquist at portrait framing, so mBump randomised the normal per fragment; (3) the mid-face mass ellipsoids sat 20-30mm in front of every feature authored on them, so eyelids, brow ridge and eye aperture never reached the zero level set — only the lips cleared it, protruding as a beak. Body, tunic, pauldron, belt and bracers now read cleanly. Face still wrong, hair is a moulded cap not a silhouette, and the sword and flute are absent.

Next action

Silhouette pass queued — hair that reads as a shape in backlit, plus the sword and flute. The face is deliberately deferred: the showcase frames Oz at distance, not in close-up.

Story, Quest & Cinematics

Original Macrion premise, the first major quest, branching dialogue, progression state, and a data-driven cutscene system with spline camera moves.

Refining iteration 2
not yet scored
no captures yet

Critic — biggest gap

VERIFIED RUNNING. story.js fully replaced with STORY.md canon — Act 0 and Act 0.5 as real quest, dialogue and interactable data. game.js written from scratch wiring eventBus, quest, dialogue and interaction. Sarah is gated behind saw_snagula so she has no presence until earned, every line of hers is true-but-incomplete for the Act III twist, and the castle-grounds fall site is planted as a landmark wired to nothing. The Act 0 to Act 0.5 chain was driven twice, once by API and once through the real E-key and proximity path. Cutscene camera authority survives all three soft-lock cases.

Next action

Player, Audio & UI

Third-person controller with terrain collision, adaptive synthesized score and ambience, and the HUD overlay. Everything audio is generated in code — no samples, no copyrighted music.

Refining iteration 2
not yet scored
no captures yet

Critic — biggest gap

HUD VERIFIED — zero HUD pixels in captures, and two real bugs fixed: toast timing used performance.now (broke determinism) and a nested play() call left the camera stuck in cutscene mode. Audio: a genuine node-graph leak fixed — sfx.js created a fresh PannerNode per positional sound and never disconnected it. Music state machine now matches spec exactly with explore/alert/combat/boss/resolve, a brass layer that only speaks in boss and combat, and stingers riding over a bed that still only cross-fades. Sarah motif written as one 9-note phrase with four arrangements: apparition, memory, ghost and wedding.

Next action

Player controller is the critical path — the animator overwrites the controller position writes each frame, so the character cannot move. Fixed first next round.

Every mesh, texture, and shader in Macrion is generated procedurally in Three.js — no asset packs, no downloaded textures. Frame captures are produced by tools/shots.mjs driving headless Chromium on the GPU, at fixed camera poses defined in docs/CAPTURE_CONTRACT.md, so every iteration is compared from identical viewpoints.

The visual bar is graded against reference frames from Final Fantasy XV and God of War, held locally and used for critique only. Those frames are copyrighted and are deliberately not reproduced on this page; the traits extracted from them are written up in docs/REFERENCE_ANALYSIS.md. The dark tick on each score track marks the 78/100 ship gate.
